name: Baruch (son of Zakkai, rebuilder of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3))
title: Rebuilder of Jerusalem's Wall
summary: Baruch, son of Zakkai, was one of the faithful Jews who participated in rebuilding Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership after the exile in Babylon. He distinguished himself through his zeal and effort, repairing a section of the wall with great dedication. His contribution is mentioned in Nehemiah 3, which documents the various workers and their assigned sections of the wall.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding of the Wall Section
keyEvents.description: Baruch, son of Zakkai, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall with great zeal under Nehemiah's leadership. He is specifically noted for working diligently on his assigned stretch.

keyEvents.title: Nehemiah's Organization of the Wall Work
keyEvents.description: Nehemiah organized the people into groups to rebuild the wall. Baruch was one of many volunteers who contributed to this national project.

keyEvents.title: The Wall Completed
keyEvents.description: Despite opposition from enemies like Sanballat and Tobiah, Jerusalem's wall was completed in just 52 days, partly thanks to the efforts of people like Baruch.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: During the work, the workers, including Baruch, faced strong opposition from surrounding peoples, but they held fast to the task with a sword in one hand and tools in the other.

keyEvents.title: The People's Commitment to God's Law
keyEvents.description: After the wall was completed, the people committed themselves to follow God's law. The rebuilders, of whom Baruch was a part, were integral to this renewal community.
